messages.subject: [JIRA] (SPARKR-126) Hide sc (SparkContext) from users
parts:
Zongheng Yang commented on SPARKR-126
 
Re: Hide sc (SparkContext) from users

I can imagine this would reduce the learning curve for R users to get to use a minimal set of SparkR APIs. However, in the long run, I'm not sure if this is a good idea: as more Spark features/APIs get added to SparkR, the inherent complexity of distributed computing would manifest itself one way or another. Hiding a familiar Spark concept in only the R API would be confusing and undermines the value of having many Spark tutorials available with more or less the same interface.

Re: Hide sc (SparkContext) from users

While I agree that we should define a high-level interface for R users, I don't think we should hide SparkContext. In terms of Spark, the SparkContext represents which cluster you are connected to – so its sort of like a first step to connect to a cluster. This may be partly addressed by the R Client package SPARKR-124 ?
